content.title: REVIEW: I cried listening to Harry Styles' new disco album
content.text: No more clowning, Harry Styles is officially back. He took an approximately two-year break from the spotlight and is now back and better than ever. Styles’ new album takes fans to a disco party and stands apart from the rest of his discography. Styles released his fourth studio album, “Kiss All The Time. Disco, Occasionally.” on March 6. This album explores Styles’ mid-life crisis, burnout and finding fulfillment beyond pop stardom. The album consists of 12 dance-pop songs and lasts about 42 minutes. “Kiss All The Time. Disco, Occasionally.” is considered a dance-pop, electronic and alternative pop album. These genres differ from those on his other three albums, which are primarily pop-rock. This new sound is not a disappointment. Styles broke his internet silence on Dec 27, 2025. He posted a YouTube video titled “Forever, Forever,” after not posting anything on YouTube for two years. This video dropping caused fan crash-outs and led to questions of what this video meant. Thankfully, the video was a sign he was coming back. Not even a month later, Styles announced his new album, and shortly followed was the first single, “Aperture.” As a fan, Styles' coming back felt like rediscovering a new, profound happiness I had once lost. I have been a big fan of Styles for as long as I can remember. He was my favorite One Direction member and I even named my car after him. I might be basic, but my love for Styles can’t compare to other artists. On my first listen to Styles’ new album, I knew it would be all I would listen to for the next week. It drew me in like a fever dream; needless to say, I’m obsessed. This album brings me so many good feelings, and there’s not a single skip. “Kiss All The Time. Disco, Occasionally.” starts with “Aperture.” Right away, it’s a song to make you get up on your feet and sing the words to your friends. It serves as a great introduction to the rest of the album, and I think it makes the perfect single. “Aperture” debuted at number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in the United States. The song expresses his desire to be back with his fans, showcasing his music and performing. I think it served as a valuable message to all of the fans who missed him. I also think this song came out in a time of hardship in our country and was a sign of hope to some people. Styles is all about love and kindness, and he came back when we needed him the most. The next song on the album, “American Girls,” immediately became my favorite song on the album. It’s a lonely song and is about how he keeps seeing his friends get married. The lyrics talk about how Styles seeks a deeper connection and misses that bond in his life. Something about it just scratches an itch I didn’t know I had. I love everything about it, and every time I listen to it, I love it more. It’s a gut-wrenching song that still has that funk sound to it. The next song, “Ready, Steady, Go!” has me popping my shoulders and bobbing my head, as do most of the songs. It’s a super upbeat song to switch up the lonesome vibes. It’s a shorter song on the album, but it hits. If you haven’t gotten up to dance to the album yet, the next track might help. “Are You Listening Yet?” will have you on your feet, feeling like a popstar. It talks about the pressure of fame, but Styles’ voice makes the song feel intentional and personal. The next two songs, “Taste Back” and “The Waiting Game,” are a bit slowed down and remind me of some of his older work. “Taste Back” goes through his emotions reconnecting with a former partner, while “The Waiting Game” I think shows his artistic choices within his career. Both songs have emotional meanings that continue throughout his album. Even though these songs have deeper meanings, they don’t stray away from the pop funk of the album. Before the album came out, the next track title had me questioning its meaning. This next song, called “Season 2 Weight Loss,” is a metaphor for how Styles is coming back stronger, improved and more confident than before. He took his break, and now he is better than ever. This song connected with me right away because I just missed Styles so much. He needed that break for his mental health, and I’m happy to see him back and doing better. Not to get more emotional, but the next song, “Coming Up Roses,” is a love song about romances that don’t last forever. As soon as this song started playing, it reminded me of the intro of “Funeral” by Phoebe Bridgers. That right there told me this song would be heartbreaking. This song just makes me want to listen to every word and take in every moment. Don’t sleep on this song because it’s slower and sadder. You can still dance to it, just slowly. After a moment of reminiscing, Styles brings in two more fun dance songs. “Pop” and “Dance No More” are two of my favorite songs on this album based on the beat and danceability. I genuinely love both of these songs so much that I can’t pick one over the other. I can literally just get up and dance around my room listening to “Pop.” It gives a new excitement that you want to hold on to. It reminds me more of his unreleased rock song “Medicine.” “Dance No More” reminds me of how dancing isn’t as normalized anymore. When I go out with my friends, I want to have fun, and that means dancing. Styles conveyed this message while giving me a new song to request at the bars. I also think “Dance No More” has my favorite lyric in the whole album. Styles sings “respect your mother” towards the end of this song, which stood out to me. Now, the second-to-last song, “Paint By Numbers,” I think, is the saddest song on the album. Some people speculate that this song is a tribute to his former band member, Liam Payne, who passed away a couple of years ago. I can see this song being about him, but some lyrics make me question if it's about a mix of people. This song makes me think about life and reminds me to make sure I’m not taking it for granted. I almost cried when I listened to this song for the first time, and it takes a lot for me to cry. The last song on the album is “Carla’s Song,” which is about Styles’ friend Carla and the experiences she had finding her love for music. Styles said this song is very important to him in interviews and talked about Carla during his one-night-only performance in Manchester.“Carla’s Song” perfectly wraps up Styles’ album. It feels like a homecoming and an appreciation of life. It turns up the mood and makes me feel more excited to listen to Harry Styles new music once again.Overall, this is a no-skip album with club beats and heartbreaking tunes. I need more listens before I say where it stands in my ranking of Harry Styles’ albums, but I give it a 10/10. I love everything about it and I think this is the album we needed.Our society needs more dance-focused albums and I hope this sets the tone for later album releases from other artists this year. It brings happiness to people and allows us to appreciate our lives.All I have to say is, thank goodness Harry Styles is back.culture@dailynebraskan.com
